subject: Anthropology
title: Marriage as Alliance
description: A short lesson to help you apply Marriage as Alliance.

hook.text: Marriage isn't just about love. For most of history, it was a treaty between groups, creating alliances and peace.

buildup.text: Anthropologists see marriage as a social institution that creates alliances between kin groups, not just individuals.

discovery.text: Levi-Strauss argued that exchanging women between groups creates bonds of reciprocity that hold societies together.

twist.text: Love-based marriage is historically rare. Arranged marriage for political and economic gain was the global norm.

climax.text: Marriage as alliance reveals that weddings are politics. Who you marry shapes power, property, and social networks.

punchline.text: Marriage ties groups together, not just people.

quiz.question: How did Levi-Strauss view marriage?
options: As exchange that creates bonds of reciprocity between groups

details.summary: Claude Lévi-Strauss argued that marriage is fundamentally about creating alliances between kin groups, not romantic love. The exchange of spouses creates bonds of reciprocity between families, clans, and communities that structure social and political life.
details.whyItMatters: Viewing marriage as alliance explains arranged marriages, bridewealth, and marriage prohibitions that seem puzzling from a Western romantic perspective. Marriage creates social bonds far beyond the couple themselves.
takeaways: Lévi-Strauss theorized marriage as alliance between kin groups
Spouse exchange creates reciprocal bonds between families
This framework explains arranged marriages and exchange systems

faq.question: What did Lévi-Strauss mean by marriage as exchange?
faq.answer: He argued that the incest taboo forces groups to exchange women with other groups, creating alliances. This exchange of spouses is a form of gift-giving that establishes reciprocal obligations between families, binding communities together through kinship.

faq.question: How does alliance theory explain marriage patterns?
faq.answer: Cross-cousin marriage, prescribed marriage partners, and marriage prohibitions all make sense as strategies for creating or maintaining alliances between specific groups. Marriage rules are social contracts, not expressions of individual preference.
